recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If future changes to unitOption/unitValueSet behavior are needed, make them in the FHIR Extension Pack; no core follow-up is needed for FHIR-37363.
issue_request: FHIR-37363 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core Questionnaire. It asked that questionnaire-unitOption and questionnaire-unitValueSet clarify that, when an answer is provided, QuestionnaireResponse.valueQuantity must match the allowed unit Coding code/system when present, fall back to Quantity.unit for display-only Codings, may warn for display/unit mismatch when code/system match, and may use $validateCode for unitValueSet validation.
initial_application: Core commit 2753aeaa5300bafb7e026272a6e12050be55a928 added the requested language to source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-extension-questionnaire-unitOption.xml and source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-extension-questionnaire-unitValueSet.xml. Those core files were later deleted by dd468d4f1799dd79819315b211588ef1cf4586e0 when extension definitions were removed from R5 source, and the Extension Pack initial import 4087c90b14dc48b4fb0d07646a6823dc1c06c22d carried forward the same guidance.
additional_context: The current core checkout actively builds Questionnaire but no longer owns the two extension StructureDefinitions; current core searches find only OID registry entries and a Questionnaire item-type definition that references the extension URLs. The active Extension Pack IG includes input/definitions/*, and its current questionnaire-unitOption and questionnaire-unitValueSet files contain the FHIR-37363 code/system/unit guidance. The linked Zulip thread supports the validation/display rationale, and the FHIR SDC 2022-07-07 minutes confirm the persuasive-with-modification decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No source hunk was made because the authoritative current extension source is already correct outside the core checkout, and duplicating the rule in the remaining core references would be unnecessary and risk drift.
